extracted.intended_audience: general readers and purchasers of 19th-century literary criticism; readers interested in Emerson/Whitman/Carlyle and art criticism
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Whitman's critical essays and jottings assessing writers (notably Carlyle) and artists, offering descriptive standards and evaluative statements about genius, poetry, philosophy, politics, and painting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's value as dislocating agitation and shock
rubrics_metrics.description: Not for his merely literary merit... but as launching into the self-complacent atmosphere of our days a rasping, questioning, dislocating agitation and shock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature's highest service is to disturb complacency and provoke rethinking; exemplified by Carlyle's ability to 'shake our comfortable reading circles' with indignation and prophetic anger rather than merely produce well-made books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic voice defined as revelation (not mere prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word prophecy... means one whose mind bubbles up and pours forth as a fountain, from inner, divine spontaneities revealing God. Prediction is a very minor part of prophecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a prophetic writer by his capacity to reveal deep inner or divine spontaneities — the outpouring of insight that reshapes moral perception — rather than by forecasting events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power as the vertebra of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Some true idea about the verteber of genius, namely power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core criterion of greatness is 'power' — an ability to command, move, and affect; genius should not be merely fashionable but possess force and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity combined with towering strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Then the simplicity and amid ostensible frailty the towering strength of this man--a hardy oak knot, you could never wear out--an old farmer dress'd in brown clothes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable character in a writer or person is the combination of simple, unpretentious outward form with resolute inner strength; such simplicity should be read as potency rather than weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring influence by imagining absence
rubrics_metrics.description: The way to test how much he has left his country were to consider... the array of British thought... but with Carlyle left out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess an author's cultural importance by imagining the intellectual landscape without them; absence-of-impact is a heuristic for gauging significance (e.g., like an army without artillery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical/systematic coherence (the Hegelian standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: All apparent contradictions in the statement of the Deific nature by different ages... are but fractional and imperfect expressions of one essential unity... a coherent metaphysical system... satisfying the mystery thereof to the human mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A philosophical system is strong when it unifies apparent contradictions into a single, illuminating conception; such coherence and the ability to console or explain the universe is a mark of philosophical success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political truth judged by just relations, not form or party
rubrics_metrics.description: Not any one party, or any one form of government, is absolutely and exclusively true. Truth consists in the just relations of objects to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate political positions by whether they maintain just relations and moral law across objects and persons, rather than by allegiance to a particular party or institutional form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic melody and philosophic clarity (Emerson)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerson... stands unmistakably at the head... sweet, vital-tasting melody, rhym'd philosophy, and poems as amber-clear as the honey of the wild bee he loves to sing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High poetic quality includes melodic language, an integration of philosophical thought with verse, and clarity and purity of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and graceful form in narrative/lyric (Longfellow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Longfellow for rich color, graceful forms and incidents--all that makes life beautiful and love refined...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poets for their capacity to render vivid color, graceful form, and refined depictions of life and love; comparative excellence on European terms is a relevant metric here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evocative natural imagery and moral threnody (Bryant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bryant pulsing the first interior verse-throbs of a mighty world--bard of the river and the wood, ever conveying a taste of open air... lurkingly fond of threnodies... chants of death... passages touching the highest universal truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poet's merit can be found in sustained interior feeling, evocative natural imagery, and the ability to engage with universal truths and elegiac tones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral energy, zeal, and rectitude in verse (Whittier)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Whittier... lives the zeal, the moral energy, that founded New England--the splendid rectitude and ardor of Luther, Milton, George Fox... the wilfulness and narrowness... the world needs... just such narrowness and wilfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess poets for moral intensity, rectitude, and zealous conviction; even narrowness or wilfulness can be a needed virtue in certain moral-poetic temperaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic originality and 'impalpable ethic purpose' in painting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before 'the Sower.' ... There is something in this that could hardly be caught again--a sublime murkiness and original pent fury... and then it seem'd to me, with that last impalpable ethic purpose from the artist (most likely unconscious to himself) which I am always looking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate paintings not only for technical finish but for a unique expressive force and an unconscious ethical purpose or moral sensibility conveyed through mood, originality, and concentrated feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for earnest conviction and moral courage in thinkers
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances... should the English-speaking world forget this man, nor fail to hold in honor his unsurpass'd conscience, his unique method, and his honest fame. Never were convictions more earnest and genuine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising thinkers or writers, give weight to the sincerity, conscientiousness, and moral courage of their convictions even when their doctrines are contested or may be disproved by time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty as a central moral/aesthetic criterion (but open to other considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second main point of Carlyle's utterance was the idea of duty being done... this formula, though precious, is rather a vague one, and that there are many other considerations to a philosophical estimate of each and every department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the principle of 'duty being done' as a stabilizing moral/aesthetic criterion, while recognizing its vagueness and the need to weigh additional philosophical or pragmatic considerations in judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of prescribing single cure-all leaders over ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The pang and hiatus of Carlyle seem to me to consist in the evidence everywhere that amid a whirl... he firmly believ'd he had a clue to the medication of the world's ills, and that his bounden mission was to exploit it... my utmost pretension is probably but to offset that old claim of the exclusively curative power of first-class individual men, as leaders and rulers, by the claims... of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating political or social prescriptions, be wary of overvaluing charismatic individual leaders as universal cures; consider the broader claims and cumulative effects of ideas and democratic processes.
